findings.description: "`pup plan` lists its goal, scope-in and acceptance criteria" is wrong: `pup plan` only prints each task's id, tier, goal headline and scope-in globs. No `pup plan` verb shows the acceptance criteria.
findings.body:
The new sentence says `pup plan` lists a task's "goal, scope-in and acceptance criteria". It does not list acceptance criteria. Bare `pup plan` runs the `list` verb (`src/cli/index.ts` L1295). That verb prints only the id, the tier, the first line of the goal (`goalHeadline`) and the scope-in globs:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/98bdbd4c3df7b6f307de95ad35184ddbc4fa0135/src/cli/index.ts#L1308-L1325

The other verbs are `add`, `drop` and `edit`. They write acceptance criteria through `--accept`, but none of them shows them. Line 15 then tells the agent to check "every acceptance criterion" for a `pup plan` task, and the command this line names never shows those criteria. An agent following it will either invent criteria or decide the task has none.

The only CLI command that prints `acceptance:` is `pup review <session>`, and it needs a session, so it does not work for a backlog task that hasn't been launched:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/98bdbd4c3df7b6f307de95ad35184ddbc4fa0135/src/cli/index.ts#L2505-L2515

Two fixes: state only what `pup plan` shows, or add a way to read a task's acceptance criteria.
findings.suggestion: If the user passes an issue number or URL, read it in full with `gh issue view <n> --comments` and state its title before starting. If the reference is ambiguous, ask. For a `pup plan` task, `pup plan` lists only its goal headline and scope-in globs, not its acceptance criteria: ask the operator for those.

findings.description: "Open the PR with `/pr-description`, writing `Closes #<n>`" contradicts `/pr-description`, which still says this repo has no tracker and the PR must carry no `Closes` line.
findings.body:
Line 17 tells the agent to open the PR with `/pr-description` and write `Closes #<n>` for an issue. This PR leaves `/pr-description` unchanged, and that skill still says the opposite:

- [L45-L48](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/98bdbd4c3df7b6f307de95ad35184ddbc4fa0135/.claude/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md#L45-L48): "**This repo has no issue tracker.** There is no ticket id in the title and no `Closes` line."
- [L170](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/98bdbd4c3df7b6f307de95ad35184ddbc4fa0135/.claude/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md#L170): "No `Closes` line: there is no tracker to close anything on."

An agent running `/implement` on an issue hands off to `/pr-description`, which tells it to drop the `Closes` line, so the issue never auto-closes. Decision 176 makes GitHub Issues the tracker, and `to-tickets` already writes `Closes #N`, so `pr-description` is the stale side. The spike plans that rewrite as T8 (`docs/spikes/2026-11-22-skills-rework.md`). T8 does not depend on T7, so nothing makes it land first, and the two skills disagree from the moment this PR merges.

Options:
- Fold T8's `pr-description` change into this PR.
- Land T8 first.
- Hold off on the `Closes` clause here until T8 lands.
